@@ -34,6 +34,12 @@ def schema_type
       schema.to_pretty_s
     end
 
+    # return a condition that is satisfied when this parameter has a value in cfg_arch
+    sig { returns(AbstractCondition) }
+    def to_condition
+      @condition ||= Condition.new({ "param" => { "name" => name, "hasValue" => true } }, @cfg_arch)
+    end
body:
Good question — looking more carefully, `Parameter#to_condition` doesn't appear to be called anywhere in the codebase. The "does this param have a value?" check is done directly in `cfg_arch.rb` via `@config.param_values.key?(p.name)`, without going through this method at all.

So the simplest fix is probably to just **remove `to_condition` entirely** from `Parameter`. It's dead code, it uses a non-existent `hasValue` operator that would raise at runtime if ever evaluated, and the underlying intent is already handled more directly elsewhere.

If there's a future use case for exposing "parameter has a value" as a condition in the DSL, that can be added properly at that time with full support in `ParameterTerm`. For now, deleting the method seems like the right call.

This drift check step is currently non-failing because the command ends with `|| true`, which overrides the `exit 1` in the failure branch. As a result, the workflow will pass even when profile configs changed. Replace with an `if git status --porcelain | grep -q .; then ...; exit 1; fi` or a `git diff --exit-code` style check so the job fails on drift.

          echo "Run `./bin/chore gen profile-cfgs`, commit the changes, and push again."
          echo "Changed files are"
